assessment: Aspiration pneumonia cohort included parkinsonism more often in one outcome group, but no food exposure or separate PD food result.

Advanced PD with dysphagia and pressure ulcers received multiple nutrition routes; semisolid tube formula after Duodopa, function/alertness and nutritional improvement during combined care. Same patient as 2020 full report given age, sex, bilateral trochanter ulcers, institution, authors and chronology.

Post-pneumonia mixed parkinsonism n136, 72 severe dysphagia. Initial dysphagia score and prior independence predicted return to three meals orally; no named food. Later Tazumi intervention report shares institution and includes the early 2015–2017 window.

One of four malnourished older adults, 89F with PD, heart failure and COPD, received MCT oil one teaspoon per meal mixed with sides then staples for 25 days with menu changes. Pooled oral nutrient fulfillment 40% to 105%; no PD-specific change, symptom, or MCT source oil.
PD outpatients H&Y 1–3, n41, 11 underweight. No clear differences in reported constipation, dysphagia, appetite or own cooking by BMI group. No individual food or preparation tested.
85-year-old woman with PD aspirated or obstructed on retained saliva. Ipratropium was the intervention; neither an obstructing food nor black pepper was involved in this abstract.

Eight post-aspiration-pneumonia older adults, diagnoses unspecified, received black pepper and menthol aroma patch for two weeks. MWST improved 2/5, WST 1/5 and RSST 1/5. No control, oral pepper or PD subgroup.
The only first-pass joint claim 0124 is a program-page co-occurrence. Separate ipratropium PD and black pepper plus menthol patch reports; see both bodies. No cracked black pepper consumption.
Utano PD two-year body-fat, autonomic symptom and ghrelin follow-up, 22 PD. Same team and measures as NHO 72 P2-4A-368; no named food exposure.

Leucine and citrulline beverage with a changed enteral regimen in 82M with PD, dysphagia and aspiration pneumonia. Pressure injury improved without resolving. Beverage administration route and subsequent swallowing measures unreported.
Utano 2018 JNS/NHO cohort again: 91 PD, 41 tube vs 36 IV-only after oral intake ceased; mean survival 809 vs 40 days. No specific formula, no new cohort.
Thirty-seven PD patients followed at least 10 years after DBS; 9 later used enteral feeding, mean 9.8 years from surgery. No specific food or formula evaluated.

Mixed neurological cases; one PD patient with dysphagia and vomiting during nasogastric feeding resumed oral intake with full lateral positioning, mixed nutrition and rehabilitation. Gained 7.6 kg and walking improved; no formula or oral food named.

Sixty-four PEG patients (10 PD) received Engelead jelly for endoscopic Hyodo scoring instead of dyed water. Outcomes grouped by severity across diagnoses, not assigned to individual PD or jelly flavor. Printed group B pneumonia count conflicts with denominator; do not use without clarification.
Case in 70s regained three independent oral meals after PEG and multidisciplinary therapy, including a half portion blended lunch, no named foods.

85M PD with variable drug swallowing tolerated full rice porridge, chopped food and thickened liquid without coughing. After training and PEG medication support later ate soft rice, bite-size chopped foods and thickened liquid. No comparison isolating ingredients or rice variety.

Drug-induced parkinsonism with terminal aspiration pneumonia and sarcopenia. Soba requested, ingredients/preparation and confirmed individual food consumption not specified; assisted oral eating lasted three days.
Pharmacist education and shared management records in specialized PD and parkinsonism homes, topics include nutrition, medication and constipation. No defined ingredient or quantified food effects.
Three Parkinson cases following aspiration-prevention surgery; surgery was the intervention. Further case-level measures from the primary PDF available.

77M PD with aspiration pneumonia and septic shock. During multidisciplinary therapy swallowing grade II-4A to II-6A, stopped tube feed day182 and discharged on full rice porridge diet. No isolated effect of rice or specific ingredients.

One stage 5 PD case. Pork mousse on day25 left marked oral/pharyngeal residue and coughing. On day36 a different meat recovery food chewed and transferred better; alternating jelly cleared residue, and later meat with tea jelly tolerated. Species/brand of second meat and tea type unreported; therapy and timing co-varied.

77M PD with sarcopenic dysphagia and aspiration pneumonia began oral Engelead jelly day3 with tube feeding and rehabilitation. Day12 residue without aspiration, day55 FOIS6 and tongue pressure 26.6 vs 21.2 kPa at day12. Apple/grape flavor and isolated jelly response unreported.

Separate 67M PD with pneumonia and sacral pressure injury, ornithine 2.5 g/day added on day79 to enteral care. Necrotic tissue absent day92; infection improved day98. Multiple wound and nutrition changes; no frozen outcome or isolated ingredient effect.
Medication workflow for levodopa and magnesium oxide in 105 PD inpatients; not an oral food intervention.
Ninety-one Parkinson outpatients. 55% normal, 37% at risk and 8% malnourished, with CONUT correlated with disease duration. No specific food exposure.
Thirty of 33 reviewed Parkinson PEG cases, with 15 eating before PEG and six after it. Two ate for at least four months. The NHO analysis uses a different count and threshold.
Utano terminal hypoglycemia analysis matches the earlier 80-person Parkinson cohort and energy means. Adds 12 of 98 in a comparison group with other diagnoses.
Original describes 23 PTEG cases, including two with Parkinson disease. The results pool diagnoses and name no food.

Tsuruta and Honma PD inpatient mood and nutrition status abstract exists in J-GLOBAL. Organizer schedule confirms oral rehabilitation nutrition session O-18-01–07; event and society archive gate bodies. No outcomes or cohort overlap established.
